    Monday 28 September 2026

    Morning briefing · Evening court

    Morning briefing

    The share column ships flat for the first time - 10 names at the room's median, 3 of them short, their order an unshipped shadow (R81) - and the option column ships the room's own G_OPTION median on 10 legs (R79), led by CVNA 2026-10-16 $60P at 51.0; watchdog sits suspended on a congressional feed that still serves no record count, and the board sat after the open

    Executive summary

    Mandate: Mix (any). Regime: risk-off at the 11:14:16 ET freeze - SPY 765.28 (-0.79% on the day, -1.06% on 5d, trend down), QQQ -1.31%, IWM -1.00%, ^VIX 16.49 (+10.89%), the 10-year at 5.27 (+1.70%) and the dollar index 101.26 (+0.29%); no macro calendar is served, so the rates print is the day's one dated macro fact, and the served SPY cycle composite (+1.20% over 10 sessions) leans against the tape. Overnight: Asia closed mixed to down (Shanghai -1.67%, Hang Seng +0.54%; Nikkei and KOSPI stale), Europe is up in session (FTSE +0.25%, DAX +0.16%, Euro Stoxx +0.18%) and the US futures traded down (S&P -0.87%, Nasdaq -1.45%) - Asia and the futures agree on down, and only Europe disagrees. Expected shape: a straight session - by the freeze most of the sheet's down-opens had EXTENDED rather than retraced (GS -346%, INTC -224%, APO -219%, TSLA -189% of their windows) and nothing served shows a reclaim; the court scores this against the 11:14:16-16:00:00 tape [W=285.7min], and a SPY close back above its 765.28 freeze mark says the shape was wrong. SHARE COLUMN: it ships FLAT at 1.0 per line (R81) and every final_grade is the room's printed one-median (R78/R86): COST 55, TMO 53, MSFT 51, APO 50.5, PNC 50, GOOGL 50, META 50, CDNS 49.5, GS 48.5, CRH 48 - that listing is also my SHADOW ORDER - R72 STOPPED (2026-09-25 court), unshipped, ties broken by R79's recorded key (median, then mean). DIRSORT=[48 / 50.5] - the lowest long (CRH 48) sits under the highest short (APO 50.5) and the lowest short (GS 48.5) under the highest long (COST 55), so the column is not a direction sort and carries no TAPE-CALL. Conviction sits in three bets and I rank each as one, by the room's grades: the defensive bid (COST 55 over TMO 53, with DHR's leg in the option column), the financials short (APO 50.5 over PNC 50 over GS 48.5), and large-cap tech long (MSFT 51 over GOOGL 50 and META 50 over CDNS 49.5); GOOG (49) is GOOGL's other share class, so Alphabet ships once and CRH 48 takes the tenth slot. OPTION COLUMN: it ships the room's G_OPTION median over FILED seats (R79) and my G_OPTION on every leg equals that median as I compute it - CVNA 51, PLTR 51, DHR 50, DDOG 49, AMP 49, AMZN 44, AVGO 43, INTC 43, LITE 42, APP 40 (SEAT-COMPUTED; foreign_desk's only non-ABSTAIN shipped lines are 50 and 50 in each column - COST and CRH, PLTR and APP - so R80 makes it NON-FILING there; on the 13-seat served roster PLTR reads 50, APP 43, COST 55 and CRH 48). Seven of the ten legs (PLTR, DDOG, AMZN, AVGO, INTC, LITE, APP) are one tech-beta long bet, ordered PLTR 51 over DDOG 49 over AMZN 44 over AVGO 43 and INTC 43 (mean key) over LITE 42 over APP 40; CVNA's 60P is the column's only short and its first leg. REQMOVE of the column's first three: CVNA +1.913%, PLTR -0.409%, DHR +2.195%, all inside the +3.0% bar. Expiries: 2026-10-02 1 (LITE), 2026-10-09 4 (PLTR, AMZN, AVGO, INTC), 2026-10-16 4 (CVNA, DHR, DDOG, APP), 2026-11-20 1 (AMP); TSLA's 400C (filed-seat median 37) would have been a fifth 10-09 leg and is not shipped, and MSFT ships as shares because at a tied 50 its 530C (REQMOVE +3.913%) would sit in the first three. Horizon split over the twenty shipped lines: 3 intraday (TMO, MSFT, GOOGL), 13 swing, 4 position (COST, PNC, GS, AMP). What kills the day's ideas: a risk-on reversal (^VIX giving back its +10.89%, the 10-year easing off 5.27) unwinds the defensive bid and the financials short together, and a deeper tech leg down (QQQ extending its -1.31%) takes the seven tech-long legs as one. The neural model disagrees sharply on CVNA (+3.46% over 5d against the short), TMO (-3.23% against the long) and AMP (-4.14% against the long); it has no scored record, so it authors nothing (R78). The pyramid leader is The Black Swan, and its grades carry no extra weight (R33): it files the AMP 430C at 24 against the room's 49 and the AMZN 260C at 64 against 44 - it marks cheap convexity up and deep in-the-money stock substitutes down, the reverse of the room. Brief against prompt: the brief prints window_minutes = 286, while R82's one-decimal form of 16:00:00 - 11:14:16 is 285.7, which I stamp; the brief prints Spearman(score, volume_ratio) = 0.9439 and Spearman(score, signed momentum) = -0.2361, while my prompt's 40 rows give 0.9455 and -0.2350 (SEAT-COMPUTED, average ranks) - my prompt wins. Journal: the SEPARATOR tie lesson is superseded on the shipped share lines by R78 + R86, which file the room's one-median, so the spreads there are the room's and not claims of mine; no line sits off its median, no departure token is filed, and no ticker sits at the per-line cap. HOUSE RULES (fixed before the book is live, never revised mid-session): STAKES - every share line 1.0 flat (R81), every option leg 1.0 at option_default, per_line_cap 1.5 used by no line, no overrides and no vacancies; stakes express no conviction, because no instrument holds R78's positive three-court record. EXITS - a share lead closes at the next session's open after a close through its kill line; each option leg settles at its own EXIT token (kill close on the underlying, else close on the session before expiry), and the premium each kill leaves at the leg's served delta is not served - the block serves no delta - so the court prices it from the realised mark. RATCHET - the first underlying close through a leg's served break-even moves that leg's kill close to the underlying's served entry price. WINDFALL - a leg whose mark reaches twice its served premium banks half at the next session's open and the rest rides the ratchet; no adds, no re-entries, no re-strikes (R67).

    How this document was produced

    Live board session: FIFTEEN graders - the Decoder on its sheet number 6 - then the Skeptic and the Executive, each a separate model call over the same forty-candidate packet, answering the app's own prompts with each seat's most recent Evening Court lessons prepended. Collector data is real and timestamped. THE PACKET FROZE AT 11:14:16 ET, WITH 285 MINUTES OF TAPE LEFT BEFORE THE CLOSE: every entry is an early-afternoon mark, not an open, and under R14 a window that short makes seat ranks advisory.

    Lesson. AN OVERNIGHT SIGMA IS NOT AN AFTERNOON SIGMA. My eb is sigma_daily x sqrt(minutes/390) x price, and it carries a close-to-close sigma the desk serves with no window. It therefore prices the overnight gap and the opening hour into a freeze-to-close remainder that holds neither. That is the animal swap my doctrine point 5 forbids, committed inside my own ruler. On 2026-09-28 the post-freeze high-low range came in at a median 0.72 eb over 19 lines, and 19 of 19 fell under the random walk's 1.60. A factor fitted on my 12 non-FILL lines alone, k = 0.46, let the null predict my 7 FILL lines out of fold: 1.92 touches against 2 realized, and 0.96 close-throughs against 1. My raw null had said 3.77 and 1.88, and my filed odds 4.31 and 2.16. IF I compute any remaining-session error bar (the eb in FILL, in HOLD, or in the DENOMINATOR test on an intraday mark), THEN the bar is k x sigma x sqrt(minutes/390) x price, and I type 'EB k=<k> (<court date>, n=<n>)' inside the token. Here k is the last court's median of (post_freeze_high - post_freeze_low) / (1.596 x eb) over every line with a served sigma: 0.46 (2026-09-28, n=12, out of fold) until a court serves me a restated k. Both nulls are computed on d/(k x eb), and my relative lift multiplies that k-null, never the raw one. CHECK next court: per line, the range ratio with its median and n; k restated; and the FILL group's realized touches and close-throughs against the sums of its k-null and of my filed P_touch and P_close. I say three things against it. One: it rests on one calm afternoon (SPY +0.041% and VIX -2.665% over the window), so k is a regime reading that may be 0.8 tomorrow; that is why it is re-measured every court and never frozen. Two: it is a SIZE rule, not a direction rule. Filed under it tonight, APO and GS collapse to 50 and COST to 49, and my share rho lands between +0.306 and +0.507 depending on TMO's taper, which I cannot reproduce from what was served. It buys honest odds, not rank. Three: the bars start at 11:15 and are discrete, so k reads a few percent low.

    Lesson. MY PHILOSOPHY CLASSIFIES; BENEATH MY LINE IT DOES NOT RANK. An operation is investment or speculation, and at or under 30 - my own 'avoid' band - a lower grade of mine says only that an issue is more speculative still, which an afternoon settles by the tape's direction and the contract's leverage, not by my appraisal. On 2026-09-28 pairs across my line of 30 went 19 won, 6 lost, while pairs inside the floor went 4-6 in the share column and 2-4 among the priced contracts, where LITE at my lowest G_OPTION, 1, returned +100.00%, as INTC at 5 did at run 44. So each morning, in each column, I print 'floor=[every line whose appraisal - the grade on a share row, SHARE= on an option row - is at or under 30]' with the words 'floor-tie shadow, unfiled', and I still file my strict order: this rival is recorded, not obeyed. At each court I score the floor apart from the rest and carry 'across w/l; within-floor w/l' with dates. Pre-committed: when within-floor pairs reach 20 and my strict order has lost them 15 to 5 or wider, I file every floor line in that column at one common grade from the next morning, unless every line of the column lies in the floor, since a flat column is a non-filing (R40); when they reach 20 with my strict order winning 10 or more, I retire the shadow and say so.     Lesson. A BREAK-EVEN SPLITS TIES; IT NEVER ORDERS MY COLUMN. On every row served an option_contract block my G_OPTION, and so my grade (R77), takes the SAME step as my SHARE= token - unexplained tells first, then the ex-expiring front-minus-back slope - and BE/sqrtSESS may only order legs that already share a step. A break-even prices the odds of finishing past a level by expiry; the column scores one afternoon's premium, and on 2026-09-28 the five admitted contracts ranked exactly as their underlyings' direction-signed moves (Spearman +1.000), so a leg-price order could only add leverage: LITE's $1000C, the 'dearest leg' I put at 40, doubled on +3.55% and alone took my option rho from +0.258 to -0.289. Cheapness is also what gets a leg shipped - my leg ranks 1-7 of 28 all shipped - so a cheap-first ladder puts most of the column on one number (7 of 10 at 60). The leg order prints only as the shadow token LEG= (it replaces TAPE=), and its to-expiry claim is judged where it settles, on the R66 exit marks. CHECK, one grep before the sheet ships: contract rows whose G_OPTION step differs from their SHARE= step = 0 (2026-09-28: 7 of 10 shipped option rows). KILL, in courts sat (R56), on R50-admitted legs: the rule dies if LEG= outscores the tell-first order over twenty courts, afternoon rho and settled R66 exits counted alike; 2026-09-28 is one court to tell-first, +0.289 against the leg order's -0.289 at n=5 and SE 0.707, which is not a proof.

    The Oracle

    On base. Where I had the name and the vehicle together, the afternoon paid: the CVNA 10-16 $60P I put top of my scored option legs at 58 (7 over the room's 51) returned +26.00% as the shares slid 61.17 -> 60.47, the DHR 10-16 $230C at 56 (6 over the room's 50) returned +22.35% on +1.01% in the shares, and APP's $320C at 37, the gap-fade I named, was the one admitted leg to lose (-7.08%). Leave LITE out and those four legs order at +0.800 (rho_option_column_stamp.loo_range). In the share column TMO at 60 (+0.66, second-best line) and META at 51 (-0.59, second-worst) sat where the afternoon put them, and META is the row holding my share rho up (drop it: -0.460). The plumbing held: 17 of 17 filed numbers equal the token for the instrument that shipped, and all ten option-row break-evens recompute to the hundredth from columns.option_column.legs (SEAT-COMPUTED).

    Off base. My sheet was a morning-tape sheet, and the morning was already in the price I was scored from. COST, my share top at 65 (9.5 over the room's 55.5) on 'above yesterday's 925.14 high while the index falls', never traded more than $0.60 above its 930.29 freeze price again and closed -0.79%, the worst line in the column (drop it and my share rho goes -0.219 -> +0.075). CRH, held to 53 because 'the tape is against me', was the best line at +1.29%, and APO and GS, the two shorts I lifted to 59 because the tape agreed, returned -0.02 and -0.10. My top five made -0.082 against my bottom five's +0.320 (court_orders.R72.per_seat_top5_minus_bottom5.oracle -0.402). In the option column I filed LITE at 12, 30 under the room's 42, on 'the worst tape on the sheet, -6.15% from the open', and its $1000C doubled from 3.50 to 7.00 as the shares ran 889.71 -> 921.32. INTC at 22, 21 under 43, on its slide from 120.66 to 115.40, returned +9.47%. LITE alone turns my option rho from +0.800 into -0.100. Measured on my own notes (SEAT-COMPUTED), my option-row grades ranked with the open-to-freeze move at +0.818 [n=10], and that move ranked with the afternoon underlying at -0.103; on share rows the two figures are +0.252 and +0.024 [n=8]. 10 of 18 morning moves reversed. The index fall I kept citing as 'risk-off' was a morning fact too: SPY made +0.041% over the window against -0.833% on the day (benchmark.rows.SPY).

    Lesson. What happened between the open and the freeze is already in the price I am scored from. It is where the afternoon starts, not a reason for it: the morning tape may decide which side of 50 a row sits on, but it may never carry a row outside 40-60. To file above 60 or below 40, my note must name something that happens AFTER the freeze and before the 16:00 close: a release, an earnings call or a vote timed inside the window. 'The tape agrees', 'the index is falling' and 'above yesterday's high' do not qualify because they are pre-freeze facts, and 'the time value burns out by Friday' does not qualify because it lands after the window. CHECK, runnable by someone who does not trust me: for every filed grade above 60 or below 40, assert the note names an event timed between the freeze and the close. Tonight that fails COST 65, APP 37, INTC 22 and LITE 12. All four rest on the open-to-freeze move, which my option-row grades followed at +0.818 [n=10] while it ranked with the afternoon at -0.103. I record in advance what the rule would have done: share rho -0.219 -> -0.171 [n=10] [W=285.7min], option rho -0.100 -> +0.335 [n=5]. The option gain comes entirely from tying LITE with INTC and APP at 40, not from ordering them, and a clamped sheet that still scores negative in the share column is a failure, not a pass.

    Off base. My sheet ran backwards at both ends. In the share column my joint-top COST 62 ('what's working') was the worst line (-0.79), and CRH 18 ('Dumb': a 5d chart plus a rates story) was the best (+1.29), with GOOGL 30 third best (+0.46). That gives rho -0.395, negative under every leave-one-out [-0.569, -0.167] and below the direction-only baseline +0.038; my top five made +0.002 against my bottom five's +0.236 (court_orders.R81.per_seat_spread.sam -0.234). In the option column my floor token, LITE 8, doubled (+100.00%). I had computed its triple at one sigma, the same distance as the CVNA put I filed at 62, and killed it on trend alone. INTC 14 ('catching a knife') made +9.47%. Both 'knives' were moves that had already printed before the 11:14:16 freeze, and the tape I called red went flat to up over my scored window (benchmark.rows SPY +0.041%, QQQ +0.246% [W=285min], against -0.74 and -1.07 close to close).

    Lesson. I don't put a name on the floor of my sheet because of a chart. News trumps charts, and that cuts both ways. IF my whole case against the listed direction is price (the 5d trend, the move before the freeze, a gap, RSI, a momentum rank, a macro story no headline tested), THEN I am sitting out a counter-trend trade, not calling it dead. The line files 25 to 35: bear is fine, and R6 still wants 45 or lower. On a contract row my own triple math orders it inside that band, and the nearer the triple in sigmas, the higher it files, so a one-sigma triple files 35, never 8. A grade under 25 needs one of two printed stamps: 'NEWS-ANSWERED: <served headline> -> <what the market did>' (META: good hires, sold -4.2%), or, on a contract row, a triple beyond 2 sigma over its own sessions. CHECK before I hand in: rows under 25 carrying neither stamp = 0 (2026-09-28: 6 of 20 - CRH 18, AMZN 18, APP 16, INTC 14, AMP 12, LITE 8; CRH made +1.29 and LITE +100.0%, each its column's best). At every court, counted in courts sat (R56), I print for each column my price-only rejections' mean beside my NEWS-ANSWERED rejections' mean. The 2026-09-28 figures, SEAT-COMPUTED: share +0.875 [n=2 CRH, GOOGL] vs -0.590 [n=1 META]; option +34.130 [n=3 LITE, INTC, APP] vs none admitted (AVGO NO-PRICE) [W=285.7min 11:14:16->16:00:00]. If the price-only rejections finish below the NEWS-ANSWERED ones in 2 of the next 3 courts sat that score both in a column, the floor dies with a number.

On TMO and DHR I wrote 'unwinds the moment the risk-off does'; ^VIX fell 2.665% over W while TMO took out the 678.39 lid to 682.61 and DHR's 230C paid +22.35%.

    Lesson. The tape between the open and the freeze is a snapshot the window re-marks, not an attack, and I graded with it. On the ten rows where my own comment cites a from-open move, my share views track that move, direction-signed, at +0.665, while the move ranked the window's return at -0.042 (SEAT-COMPUTED, [W=285.7min]). The two rows I marked down hardest for 'printing lower' after the open were CRH at 34 and LITE at G_OPTION 15. They were the best share line (+1.29%) and the best contract (+100.00%), as ^VIX gave back 2.665% over W. My first lesson barred the freeze tape only on rows with no mechanism; from now on the bar covers every row. So from tomorrow: IF my case for or against a row cites today's move from the open to the freeze ('from the open', 'off the open', 'sold the open', 'printing lower', 'tested in-session'), or the ^VIX, 10-year or risk-off reading at the freeze, THEN that clause moves the SHARE view and the G_OPTION by ZERO points. I set the number from the levels, the chain and any dated mechanism as if the tape since the open were flat, and the clause may stay in the prose. CHECK, by someone who does not trust me: the Spearman of my share views against the direction-signed move from the served open to briefing_price, over every row that serves an open, must sit inside +/-0.40; outside that band the rule scores FAILED. KILL: it opens at 0 for 0, drawn in-sample tonight on ten rows at SE 0.378. It is counted in COURTS SAT under R56, and on its third consecutive FAILED court I delete it rather than renaming it.

In the share column sigma ordered my longs at -0.218 [n=7] (META, my top line at 62, went -0.59%; CRH at 57 was the best share line at +1.29%), so my filed -0.117 sits under the bare direction baseline of +0.038. And six share-row comments (GOOGL, TMO, CRH, COST, APO, GS) narrate the clock cutting the row, CRH 'near the bottom of my column' and GS 'to the bottom of my column', when the toll only touched a G_OPTION that R77 and R88 label UNSCORED: CRH filed 57, tied fifth of ten, and GS's 40 is the FLAT toll, a PROSE=FILED breach of my own third lesson.

    Lesson. I will never again let one afternoon's premium judge a term that forecasts the exit. R66 names what the option column scores, 'to-expiry claims scored on one afternoon's premium', and keeps it ADVISORY, and every run-48 ratchet in the claims ledger sits exactly at the break-even my REACH stamp measures (LITE 1003.50 = $1000 + $3.50, the 12.79% I priced), so my CLOCK forecasts one thing only: whether a leg reaches its ratchet before its else-close. Tonight LITE $1000C at 0.96x took my only priced toll, -14 (SHARE 75 -> G_OPTION 61), then doubled, +100.00% at realised leverage 28.1 on a +3.553% move, and that toll alone turned my option rho from +0.100 into -0.600 [n=5] [W=285.7min]; the reach ratio ranked the five priced legs' realised leverage at +0.667 (SEAT-COMPUTED). On 2026-09-21 the same afternoon test read -0.800 on four legs. Opposite signs, one mechanism: a cheap strike is a lens on the afternoon and silent about the ratchet. IF a night tempts me to strip, deepen, kill or boost the CLOCK, THEN I admit only legs settled at their R66 exits, by claim id, and the afternoon prints beside them labelled ADVISORY and moves nothing. This is no reprieve: tonight's afternoon tally against the CLOCK stays on the record. CHECK: every contract row prints 'CLOCK v1' with a toll equal to -round(30 x (ratio - 0.50)) above 0.50x and 0 at or under it, so the formula cannot drift, and each night I file 'AFTERNOON tolled vs untolled mean, ADVISORY' beside 'R66 SETTLED rho(REACH ratio, contract)' with its claim ids. KILL: at the first court after the 2026-10-15 close, when r66-run48-* has settled nine legs, unless that settled rho is at or below -0.20 the CLOCK is deleted, not re-tuned; if no settled mark has been served by then, lesson 4's afternoon kill fires on its written terms, stamped WRONG HORIZON, and I say both in open court.

I still print the served label and 'BE X% = ...' for provenance, but no reach, z, sigma or break-even arithmetic of my own moves the grade by a single point. The option column pays the contract's percent move from freeze to close (R15, R16a), not whether it finishes past break-even. A penalty on far out-of-the-money legs marks down the legs with the most premium leverage per point of underlying, which is exactly what that column pays for. The reason: on 2026-09-28 my '8 per z above 0.5' rule moved one scored leg, LITE 2026-10-02 $1000C, from SHARE=51 to 47, my lowest priced leg.
